vision:
A Library should read like one series from a good university press, carried onto the screen. Every volume shares the same trim, typeface, running head, contents, folios and apparatus. Each book is told apart only by its cover: its four colours and field from book.json, the figure on its front door, and, for the two instruments, the masthead they keep on wide screens. Today the four books look like four websites: four type systems, four theme controls, two stat styles, nine micro-label styles, and apparatus classes leaking between page types. The system replaces that with one frame and one inset, one type system (serif for what is read, sans for what is operated, weights declared as they actually render), colour roles derived from each book's own paper and ink in both themes, one label vocabulary, one 'has a card' mark, and a vertical rhythm measured in lines of the book's own text.

Navigation should feel like holding a book. The library bar is the running head on every page, the hub included, full-bleed at one inset so its brand never moves. It carries the book's name, its destinations under one name each, Library, and the only theme control; on a phone it keeps one row and folds the destinations under Menu. In a book there are three moves, each one step away on every device. Up: Library, the brand, the sidebar's '← Part XII' breadcrumb, or the same breadcrumb as the drawer's first row on a phone. Across: previous and next, always labelled with the chapter number, in the sidebar's folio row, the chapter foot, the phone folio bar and the arrow keys. Back: the browser or the installed app's back control. While the reader reads down, chrome recedes, and it returns only on a deliberate scroll up, at the chapter's end, or on request. A returning reader is met where they left off: a sequential book promotes Continue to its front door's primary action, while the clinical reference keeps Contents first and offers Continue beside it.

The oncologist between patients gets evidence tables that use the whole screen and fold trial identity into the first cell. Every cell names its column on a phone, and the page offers trial cards, collapsed references that still print, a 'Find a chapter' box on the contents, and a theme that never flips under them. The self-taught physics reader gets inline maths that is never shrunk, displays that fit or scroll with cues, equation numbers in the margin, equation references that preview the equation without losing the place, sitting breaks that read, a Through-Line at a true reading measure, and a sidebar that tracks where they are. Under all of it sits a harness that measures what it claims to measure, and every stage degrades safely: the Dropbox build, a new page on an old installed shell, and an old page on a new one.
principles: The page is the book and the chrome is the binding. Chrome recedes while the reader reads down, and returns on a deliberate scroll up (48px or a flick), at the chapter's end, or on request.

One of everything: one bar at one inset, one theme control, one name per destination, two label styles (an accent kicker and a grey label), one link style, one 'has a card' mark (the dotted underline), one focus ring, one 'you are here' mark.

Identity comes from colour, figure and masthead, not layout. accent, accent_dark, ink, paper and field are the only values that differ; front doors keep their figures, and the instruments keep their masthead lockup at 1000px and wider.

Serif for what is read: titles, headings, prose, questions, chapter titles, trial names in prose, the instruments' dossier text. Sans for what is operated: navigation, labels, table cells, captions and controls. Weights are declared as they render: serif 400/400i/700, sans 400/600/700.

No word falls below 4.5:1 in either theme, measured by a census that reads every colour syntax and fails on any it cannot read. De-emphasise with size, weight or position, never paler ink or opacity. Hairline colours are never text.

Nothing moves unless the reader moved it. The theme is final at first paint, bar items never shift between page types or when scripts arrive, and prefers-reduced-motion is honoured everywhere, including scrolling.
Every control works by thumb (44px under pointer:coarse) and by keyboard (visible focus, a skip link, DOM order matching visual order), without flooding the tab order.
Up, across and back are always one step away on every device, and 'across' always names the chapter it goes to.
Facts are built, not typed. Counts, labels, neighbours, positions and start chapters come from book.json, the curriculum and the data files, at build time where possible.

Presentation only. No prose, trial fact, reference or registry data changes, proven by a text diff with stated rules. Offline and PWA behaviour stay whole, the checks stay green, and new UI copy uses no em dash.
Every stage degrades safely. The Dropbox build, a new page on an old installed shell, and an old page on a new shell each keep a working theme control and chapter navigation.
Measure before and after. Every 'was N' has a wave-0 baseline, and every wave ends with a gate on the merged tree that includes the physics book.

- Light:

  - bg-alt = ink 4.5%;
  - paper = #fff 65% into bg;
  - ink-soft = ink 76% (7.05 / 7.00:1 on bg-alt, clinical / physics);
  - ink-faint = ink 68% (5.36 / 5.31 on bg-alt; the palest word colour);
  - rule 13% and rule-soft 7% (hairlines only);
  - accent-soft = accent 10%;
  - accent-line = accent 45% into transparent.
- Dark: the block redeclares every role whose light formula is wrong on a dark ground.
  - bg = accent_dark 5% into #15171b;
  - paper = #fff 3% into bg (a raised surface is a shade lighter; the old formula gave 1.65:1);
  - ink = #e2e1dc;
  - ink-soft 74% (6.93 or better on paper);
  - ink-faint 60% (4.86 or better on bg-alt, 4.99 or better on paper);

- Every filled component sets --surface to its own ground; scroll cues paint in it.

THEME
- BOOT resolves library:v1.look (written only by a press), then nmt-theme, then prefers-color-scheme, before first paint, and adds html.js. library:v1.theme is never read.
- Control: button.nav-theme, last in the bar on every barred page including the hub.
  - Half-filled circle SVG; aria-pressed; aria-label 'Dark theme'; title 'Switch to dark/light'; 36px, or 44px under touch.
  - It ships hidden. pwa.js removes hidden, wires it and sets html.theme-wired. nav.css reserves its slot under html.js, so nothing shifts.
- A press: flip data-theme, save look, sync theme-color, dispatch window 'library:theme'. book.js redraws on the event and on data-theme mutation.
- Fallback: book.js builds the floating #themer (writes nmt-theme) only when html.theme-wired is absent at window load. That covers the Dropbox build and an old installed shell. With no BOOT, book.js stamps nmt-theme or the OS setting (no forced light).
- continue.html and offline.html resolve the theme the same way inline.

LAYOUT
- Breakpoints:
  - 1500: chapter block centres;
  - 1200: margin track and table bleed;
  - 1000: sidebar vs phone chrome;
  - 640: phone type and bar Menu;
  - 430: narrowest.
- One inset: nav.css --lib-inset (1.25rem, or 1rem below 640px) is read by the bar, the sidebar and every frame's inner gutter. The bar is full-bleed on every page and reads no frame width, so the brand x is constant library-wide and equals the sidebar text x. There is no --lib-frame.
- --lib-bar-h is 2.75rem at every width, plus env(safe-area-inset-top) when installed. The Dropbox build sets it to 0px after the inlined nav.css.
- Page-level rules:
  - html, body use overflow-x:clip (hidden only as the @supports fallback), and the masked sweep is the overflow test.
  - scroll-padding-top = bar height + .75rem.
  - Smooth scroll only under no-preference.
- z-index scale (--lib-z-*): bar 40, folio 40, menu 45, scrim 50, sheet 60, card 70, toast 80. The toast sits above the folio.
- Page types:
  - Hub (content frame 64rem): bar; lede; Continue strip; tiles in 2 columns at 640px and up; storage line; footer.

    - The column is 35em.
    - --breakout is a registered length, at most 18rem, for hanging equation numbers and wide figures.
    - .main is an inline-size container. .col > .evidence bleeds from the column's left edge to .main's right content edge (100cqi against 100%). At 1500px and up it spans the whole of .main, symmetric about the centred column-and-margin block.

  - Chapter, below 1000px: sticky bar with headroom; full-width column; fixed folio bar; the drawer as a bottom sheet.

NAVIGATION MODEL
- Between books: the bar's Library link, hub tiles and the Continue strip.
- Into a book: tile, then front door, then primary: 'Begin / 0.1 …' or 'Continue reading' (physics), or Contents (clinical).
- Within a book: bar destinations (Menu at 640px and below), .go links, contents rows and 'Find a chapter', arc rows to contents#sec-N.
- Up: the sidebar '← Part' or the drawer's first row to contents#sec-N; the bar brand to the front door.
- Across: sidebar ‹ 67 · 69 ›, foot cards, folio ‹ 67 · 69 ›, drawer cards, and the ← → keys.
- Within a chapter: the spy TOC, the folio label, drawer sections and equation cards.
- Back: the browser, or .pwa-back when installed.
- Resume: the hub strip, the front door, 'Last read' on the contents page, continue.html?b=.
- One name per destination: Contents, In Plain Terms, Math Ledger, Stories, Trial Registry (eyebrow 'Appendix A'), Library. The ledger's eyebrow is the book title.
- A book with nothing written builds no contents page.

CONTRACTS
- Text-pass anchors: bare <body>; the viewport meta string is unchanged.
- book.js boot shape (runtime_js):
  - the handler keeps numberEquations(); first and ends with the katex if/else;
  - new calls go between them;
  - layout-dependent features register their own listeners outside the handler.
  - Both runtime_js() copies raise unless each substitution happens exactly once.
- Build capture: every book.js insertion inside .col or #sb-toc is idempotent or lives outside them, and no state class is saved.
- Bar: data-book = slug; pwa.js sets ROOT='../' when it is present; the buttons ship hidden and pwa.js sets html.theme-wired.
- nav.css defines only --lib- tokens: serif, sans, mono, bar-h, inset and z-*.
- --breakout is a registered length. .main is an inline-size container at 1200px and up.
- nav.json gains 'reading'.
- Sidebar: .sb-home and .sb-folio (a.sb-prev, p.sb-title, a.sb-next). .chapnav a.prev/a.next are the neighbour source.
- Contents: h2.part-head#sec-i from build.py; .clist li; li[data-last] with span.tag.last; .toc-head.
- Drawer selectors: #mnav, #mnav-btn, .mn-up, .mn-kicker, .mn-title, .mn-list, .mn-seq .prev/.next .mn-ch, .mn-seq > span.
- Front door: .cta > .btn with .btn-main and .btn-sub; the START placeholders.
- Theme: window 'library:theme'. Stored keys library:v1.look and library:v1.lastBy[slug] = {url, num, title, pct, at}.
- bc.py markup: span.trial[data-trial]; span.trial.chip; p.ev-title and p.ev-note; td[data-label]; span.m[data-col]; story-<id>; details.refs-list. Registry rows keep id t-<key>; #SQ- ids stay on the questions.
- Offline listing: a book counts only when its __resident__ entry has complete:true.

MEASURING AND GATES
- Every docs-touching run goes through scratchpad/ui/architect/locked.sh (flock). Each package uses its own NAVCHECK_PORT.
- contrast.js was fixed in revision 2 to read color(srgb …) and canvas-paintable colours. Pass = failing 0 AND unparsed 0 AND measured at or above the page's wave-0 baseline.
- Repo checks:
  - nav.py --check; pwa.py --check (wave 0 makes it compare regenerated PAGE, manifests and nav.json); sitecheck.py (wave 0 adds SITE-prefixed hrefs and #fragments, and --build <slug>); navcheck.py (wave 0 makes waits fail rather than abort, and adds the masked overflow sweep).
  - make.py plus verify.py for BOTH books; figcheck.py on newton-to-mtheory/ch*; bc.py --check when bc.py changes.
- Physics verify may exceed its baseline only by the displays in baselines/eq-wide.json, until W4-MATH.
- Wave gate on the merged tree:
  - rebuild what the wave touched;
  - run all checks, the contrast census, mixshell.py and the proof-page shots;
  - the architect reviews before the next wave.
- Only Chromium is installed, and the screenshots render Bitstream Charter and DejaVu Sans. Wave 0 attempts WebKit; otherwise W5 writes a review of every @supports fallback.
- Waves: 0 harness; 1 HEAD, TOKENS, PHILO; 2 FRAME, PHONE; 3 CLINIC, FM, HUB; 4 MATH; 5 INTEGRATE. Everything is on one UI branch, and docs/ reaches main only after W5.
